title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1969-06-21
lineage: Early Show: AUD > MR > C > R > R > R > D > CD > EAC > SHN; Late Show: SBD > MC > C > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Muddy audience first set vs. crisp soundboard second set, but the show shines with rare Old Old House, wild China Cat and a smoking King Bee.
ai_review.review: The recording is split – an almost unlistenable audience tape of the first set followed by a clean, complete sound‑board capture of the second. Musically the night is a gem: early acoustic numbers, a historic debut of “Mama Tried,” a wild “China Cat” jam, a rare “Old Old House,” and a smoking “King Bee.” Despite the first‑set audio flaws, the performance’s energy and rarity make it worth listening.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is high with many standout, historic performances; recording quality is uneven (muddy audience tape vs. crisp soundboard), pulling the overall rating to solid‑plus.

recording_quality.technical_notes: First set is an audience tape – muddy and difficult to follow. Second set is a clear, crisp soundboard recording but only covers the latter half of the concert.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Starts with an acoustic half‑set and early country/folk numbers, then shifts into full‑band psychedelia; the second set picks up in energy and sound quality.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Pedal steel work highlighted on “China Cat” and “Love Light”; his guitar tone described as wild and ripping.
band_member_comments.Bob: Lead vocal on “Dire Wolf” noted as a standout moment.
band_member_comments.Keys: Prominent pedal‑steel/keyboard textures praised throughout, especially in the acoustic portions.
